        ### Question
        A 55-year-old woman who works as a chef is brought to the hospital for evaluation of burns sustained in a kitchen accident. Physical examination reveals 3rd-degree burns over the anterior surface of the right thigh and the lower limbs, which involve approx. 11% of the total body surface area (TBSA). opb. Early excision and split-thickness skin grafting
opc. Delayed excision and skin grafting
opd. Topical antibiotic application of mafenide acetate
ope. Fluid resuscitation with Ringer’s lactate solution per the Parkland formula

CHAIN: "Weak dorsalis pedis pulses" -> "possible compromised circulation" -> "monitoring and resuscitation needed" -> "fluid resuscitation with Ringer’s lactate" -> 85%
